home.hero_sub: Harvest Compass tells a farmer which mandi pays the most once transport is paid for, and which days are dry enough to harvest. Wheat, paddy, soybean, onion, potato, pulses, vegetables and more. Ask in English, Hindi or 21 other Indian languages, by voice or text.

home.problem_title: Most farmers sell at the nearest mandi, or wherever a trader says.
problems: Prices differ from mandi to mandi, and the trip to reach a better one costs money.
Published prices can be days old, or come from one odd lot that doesn't represent the market.
Rain on harvest or transport day spoils the crop. Forecasts exist, but in English and in millimetres.

gets.d: The mandi that pays most after round-trip transport at the farmer's own vehicle rate, not the one with the highest headline price.
Days inside the harvest window when ECMWF and GFS both expect it to stay dry, and the transport day after.
What waiting three days might do, from the real 14-day price trend and rain risk, labelled as a trend, not a forecast.
Which Rampur? How many kg in a sack? What does the vehicle cost? One short question instead of a made-up value.

home.audit_body: Public price data is messy. Before ranking, the agent rejects prices that are stale, inconsistent, far from the mandi's own recent history, or for a different variety, and names each mandi it dropped with the reason. The language model only phrases numbers the agent computed; a checker throws out any number or mandi name it can't find in the facts.
home.audit_link: How the audit and repair work
home.audit_caption: Real lines from the agent's log, 31 Oct 2026: 40 quintals of soybean near Ujjain.
home.measured_body: We replayed 60 days of real prices for 30 real villages in Madhya Pradesh. Each day the agent chose using only what it would have known that day; we then scored it on the next day's real price against simply going to the nearest mandi. Transport assumed at ₹1 per quintal per km.

how.title: One question, seven steps, all on screen.
how.sub: Harvest Compass is a LangGraph agent. The language model reads the question and phrases the answer. Everything between, including every rupee, is plain code you can check.

loop.name: Understand
loop.body: A language model turns the question, in English, Hindi or any of 21 other Indian languages, into a strict form: crop, quantity, village, harvest window, vehicle rate. Sacks need a stated weight. If the village matches two places, or a value is missing, it asks one short question.

loop.name: Plan
loop.body: Plain rules decide which sources to call and why: today's prices, 30 days of history, two weather models, road routes. A question about waiting adds the trend step.

loop.name: Fetch
loop.body: Calls run in parallel with timeouts and one retry. Every response is cached with its source URL and fetch time, so a later failure can fall back to real older data and say how old it is.

loop.name: Audit
loop.body: Pure rules, no model: prices older than 3 days, min above max, outliers against the mandi's own month and the region, and mismatched variety or grade are excluded. Each rejection is shown with its reason.

loop.name: Repair
loop.body: If too few mandis survive, the search radius widens. If today's price feed is down, each mandi's latest report is used with its age. If one weather model is down, the other is used and days are marked uncertain.

loop.name: Calculate
loop.body: Each mandi's 7-day median price minus round-trip transport (trips × 2 × km × the farmer's rate) gives net ₹ per quintal. A farther mandi has to win by more than ₹50 a quintal to beat a nearer one.

loop.name: Explain
loop.body: The model writes two or three sentences in the farmer's language from the computed facts only. A checker rejects any number or mandi name not in the facts, retries once, then falls back to a fixed template. Sarvam reads it aloud.

how.rules_body: A rejected mandi is never silently dropped. The farmer sees it under "Mandis left out" with the reason.

rules.v: Price reported more than 3 days ago
Minimum above maximum, or the modal price outside the min–max range
Unusual against both the mandi's own last 30 days and today's regional prices (robust z-score)
Different variety or grade from the most common lot in the region
Mandi town not found on OpenStreetMap, so no honest road distance

how.switches_body: On the ask page, the test switches let anyone turn a source off for the next question: today's prices, one weather model, routing. The agent skips it and the log shows how it recovers.
how.voice_body: Sarvam speech-to-text turns the recording into text in the chosen language (all 22 scheduled languages and English), which lands in the box so the farmer can fix a misheard word. The reply is spoken by Sarvam text-to-speech in the 9 languages it has voices for; the rest get text. If the mic is blocked or speech fails, typing and reading still work.

results.bt_title: Backtest: 60 days, 30 villages in Madhya Pradesh
results.bt_body: Each day, the agent chose a mandi using only data up to that day, with its own audit and ranking. We scored the choice on the next day's real price at that mandi, against the nearest reporting mandi. Regret is how far behind the best mandi in hindsight it was.

limits: Transport in the backtest is an assumed range, not a measured local rate. Live answers use the farmer's own rate.
data.gov.in history lags a day and many mandis skip days; about 30–40% of replayed decisions couldn't be scored.
The ₹50 per quintal close-call margin is a judgement call.
Only mandis in the farmer's own state are compared.
Weather beyond 7 days isn't forecast; those days are shown as having no forecast yet.
Voice accuracy on real farmer recordings is still being measured.

data.fee_body: In Madhya Pradesh, under the Krishi Upaj Mandi Adhiniyam 1972, section 19(2), the buyer pays the market fee and it can't be deducted from the farmer's price, so the seller's fee is zero. Other states set their own rules, so there the answer notes that the market fee is not included. Hammali and weighing charges are set by each mandi committee, so the farmer enters them if they pay them; nothing is assumed.
data.vehicle_body: There's no public source for local truck and tractor hire, so the agent asks the farmer for their rate per km and how many quintals one trip carries. Both can be edited on the answer to recalculate.
data.fail_body: The agent falls back to the latest real stored data and states its age, or to the other weather model, and lowers its confidence. It never fills a gap with a made-up value.
data.privacy_body: Questions and the agent's steps are logged to measure speed and reliability. IP addresses and identities are not stored.

about.title: Public data, put to work for the person who grows the crop.
about.p1: India publishes daily prices from mandis across the country, and global weather models are free to use. But this data is scattered, in English, unchecked, and shaped for analysts. A farmer with 40 quintals still decides with a phone call to a trader.
about.p2: Harvest Compass brings that data to one question asked in the farmer's own language, checks it before trusting it, and shows its working. It covers the crops data.gov.in reports, from wheat and paddy to vegetables, for any village in India, using the mandis that report in the farmer's state. Built for FORGE '26.
